### N-23 — fixed (CONFIRMED)

**Probe Q1** (`s1/probe/probe.ts`, the hook above). It ran on the flat fixture at plain size and at 900 ha, seeds
1 – 30 each, 60 runs per copy. Every street whose first segment leaves a standing `through` / `primary` way was found
from the hooked feature index. Its dead end was taken from its last `legal` call: a rejection after n accepted steps
is a dead end at step n + 1. The cause is the feature that call cites. The cited street is *farSide* when its own first
segment leaves the same arterial on the other side; this is classified from geometry, never from the code's `origin`.
The counts include streets the between-stage prune later removes, so they are larger than C-0263 (3)'s, which are
taken after the prune. The post-prune single-segment counts below reproduce C-0263 (3) exactly.

| … vs the far-side street at any step | 410 | **0** | 374 | **0** |
| all arterial-street dead ends at step 2 – 3 | 579 | 214 | 553 | 208 |
| arterial streets with one step | 568 | 154 | 556 | 181 |

| S5c streets after prune; single-segment | 1 448; 390 | 1 721; 169 | 1 444; 354 | 1 695; 190 |
| arterial streets with a later step and no `origin` on it | — | 0 | — | 0 |

**V02 under N-48 (note N-24, KI).** V02 survives NEAR (`Tests 136 passed (136)`, 546 s) and changes S5's committed
output on 15 of 30 fixture runs (plain 2: 60 → 61 streets, 3: 55 → 57, 4: 59 → 54, …). Probe Q1 run under V02 (copy
`s1/diagV02`) puts its effect at **39 + 39 arterial streets dead at step 3 against the far-side street**, where the tree
has 0 + 0. So the "whole life" part of C-0263 (1), beyond the second step, has no pinning test. The growth 0.9-pitch
test checks only stubs of up to two steps, and the legality tests use `steps: 1`.

The seat's probe CONFIRMS the code correct on this promise: 0 far-side dead ends at any step on 60 runs. The gap leaves
no test id or exit bar of `M0-work.json` unproven. It is not a fail-safety, persisted or contract class either: the
mutant only rejects more steps. N-48 therefore makes it a KI test-gap note rather than a blocker. The brief's own
example, "exemption on the first step only", is V01 and is killed. **This is the seat's vetoable call.** The stricter
reading ("a survivor on a stated promise stays a blocker") would fail the item on a tests-only fix: one more growth
assertion, given in N-24.

The other survivors change no fixture output. V09 and V19 are equivalent by reasoning, and V14 is equivalent in
practice. V08, V10, V12 and V12b reach only contrived sub-centimetre or rare shapes. All of them are in notes N-25 and
N-26.

**Soundness of the exemption (PLAUSIBLE, by reasoning).** The skip never opens a thin strip. It needs the parent way
to lie between the step and f where they come nearest, and the parent way keeps its own clearance against the step
(it is a standing feature, exempt only where it holds the step's start). A step running beside the arterial inside
the clearance is therefore still rejected against the arterial itself. If a misread or reversed-run side compares two
same-side streets as opposite, `wayBetween` still refuses the skip, because the way does not lie between them (V05,
V03 killed).
